        "[" [ BooleanExpression ] "]" 
            ( ( TimeoutStatement |
               ReceiveStatement |
               TriggerStatement |
               GetCallStatement |
               CatchStatement |
               CheckStatement |
               GetReplyStatement |
               DoneStatement |
               KilledStatement ) StatementBlock ) 
             | 
            ( AltstepInstance [ StatementBlock ] )
       } 
       [ "[" else "]" StatementBlock ]
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement denotes branching of test behaviour due to the reception and handling of communication events, timer events and/or the termination of parallel test components, using the operations `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`, `check`, `timeout`, `done` and `killed`.
requirements.original: The alt statement denotes branching of test behaviour due to the reception and handling of communication and/or timer events and/or the termination of parallel test components, i.e. it is related to the use of the TTCN-3 operations receive, trigger, getcall, getreply, catch, check, timeout, done and killed.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement denotes a set of possible events that are matched against a particular snapshot.
requirements.original: The alt statement denotes a set of possible events that are to be matched against a particular snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement MAY define local definitions before its alternative branches.
requirements.original: An alt statement may define some local definitions before its alternative branches.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.canonical: A local definition of an `alt` statement CAN be used by all branches of that `alt` statement.
requirements.original: These can be used by all the branches.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.condition: an alt statement is entered
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement is entered, a snapshot IS taken.
requirements.original: When entering an alt statement, a snapshot is taken.

requirements.subject: ent:local-definition
requirements.condition: the alt statement contains local definitions
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement contains local definitions before its first branch, the local definitions ARE evaluated before the snapshot is taken.
requirements.original: If the alt statement contains local definitions before its first branch, these are evaluated before the snapshot is taken.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: a repeat statement is executed in the alt statement
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement executes the `repeat` operation, the whole `alt` statement, including its local definitions, IS re-evaluated.
requirements.original: When the alt statements executes the repeat operation, the whole alt statement, including the local definitions, is re-evaluated.

ambiguity.issue: "repeat operation" is used, while clause 20.3 names it the repeat statement; also "alt statements executes" is grammatically garbled.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The alternative branches of an `alt` statement, the top alternatives of invoked altsteps and the top alternatives of altsteps activated as defaults ARE processed in the order of their appearance.
requirements.original: The alternative branches in the alt statement and the top alternatives of invoked altsteps and altsteps that are activated as defaults are processed in the order of their appearance.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: several defaults are active
requirements.canonical: If several defaults are active, the top alternatives of the defaults ARE evaluated in the reverse order of the activation of the defaults.
requirements.original: If several defaults are active, the reverse order of their activation determines the evaluation order of the top alternatives in the defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The alternative branches in active defaults ARE reached by the default mechanism.
requirements.original: The alternative branches in active defaults are reached by the default mechanism described in clause 20.5.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.condition: the alt statement contains the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, all active default alternatives ARE ignored for the execution of that `alt` statement.
requirements.original: If the alt statement contains the @nodefault modifier, all active default alternatives are ignored for the execution of this alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: An alternative branch IS either a branch that may be guarded by a Boolean expression or an else-branch, i.e. a branch starting with `[else]`.
requirements.original: The individual alternative branches are either branches that may be guarded by a Boolean expression or else-branches, i.e. alternative branches starting with [else].

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: the else-branch is reached
requirements.canonical: An else-branch IS always chosen and executed when it is reached.
requirements.original: Else-branches are always chosen and executed when they are reached (see below).

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: A branch that may be guarded by a Boolean expression IS either an altstep-branch (invoking an altstep), a done-branch (starting with a `done` operation), a killed-branch (starting with a `killed` operation), a timeout-branch (starting with a `timeout` operation) or a receiving-branch (starting with a `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` or `check` operation).
requirements.original: Branches that may be guarded by boolean expressions either invoke an altstep (altstep-branch), or start with a done operation (done-branch), a killed operation (killed-branch), timeout operation (timeout-branch) or a receiving operation (receiving-branch), i.e. receive, trigger, getcall, getreply, `catch or a check operation.

ambiguity.issue: Editorial: misplaced backticks span across this sentence and the next one in the source.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a Boolean guard SHALL be based on the snapshot.
requirements.original: The` evaluation of the Boolean guards shall be based on the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: A Boolean guard IS considered fulfilled if no Boolean guard is defined or if the Boolean guard evaluates to `true`.
requirements.original: The Boolean guard is considered to be fulfilled if no Boolean guard is defined, or if the Boolean guard evaluates to true.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled
requirements.canonical: An altstep-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled.
requirements.original: An altstep-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of an altstep-branch causes the invocation of the referenced altstep, and the evaluation of the snapshot continues within the altstep.
requirements.original: The selection of an altstep-branch causes the invocation of the referenced altstep, i.e. the altstep is invoked and the evaluation of the snapshot continues within the altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.canonical: An altstep-branch MAY contain an optional statement block.
requirements.original: An altstep-branch may contain an optional statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.canonical: The optional statement block of an altstep-branch SHALL be executed only if an alternative of the altstep referenced in the altstep-branch has been selected and executed.
requirements.original: The optional statement block shall be executed only, if an alternative of the altstep referenced in the altstep-branch has been selected and executed.

requirements.subject: ent:done-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the component is in the stopped list of the snapshot
requirements.canonical: A done-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified test component is in the list of stopped components of the snapshot.
requirements.original: A done-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of stopped components of the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:done-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a done-branch causes the execution of the statement block following the `done` operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the done operation.

requirements.subject: ent:done-operation
requirements.canonical: A `done` operation in a selected done-branch has no further effect beyond the selection of the branch.
requirements.original: The done operation itself has no further effect.

requirements.subject: ent:killed-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the component is in the killed list of the snapshot
requirements.canonical: A killed-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified test component is in the list of killed components of the snapshot.
requirements.original: A killed-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified test component is in the list of killed components of the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:killed-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a killed-branch causes the execution of the statement block following the `killed` operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes the execution of the statement block following the killed operation.

requirements.subject: ent:killed-operation
requirements.canonical: A `killed` operation in a selected killed-branch has no further effect beyond the selection of the branch.
requirements.original: The killed operation itself has no further effect.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot
requirements.canonical: A timeout-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the specified timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot.
requirements.original: A timeout-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the specified timeout event is in the timeout-list of the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a timeout-branch causes the execution of the specified `timeout` operation, i.e. the removal of the timeout event from the timeout-list, and the execution of the statement block following the `timeout` operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes execution of the specified timeout operation, i.e. removal of the timeout event from the timeout-list, and the execution of the statement block following the timeout operation.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-branch
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled and the matching criteria are fulfilled
requirements.canonical: A receiving-branch IS selected if its Boolean guard is fulfilled and the matching criteria of the receiving operation are fulfilled by one of the messages, calls, replies or exceptions in the snapshot.
requirements.original: A receiving-branch is selected if the Boolean guard is fulfilled and if the matching criteria of receiving operation is fulfilled by one of the messages, calls, replies or exceptions in the snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-branch
requirements.canonical: The selection of a receiving-branch causes the execution of the receiving operation, i.e. the removal of the matching message, call, reply or exception from the port queue, possibly an assignment of the received information to a variable, and the execution of the statement block following the receiving operation.
requirements.original: The selection causes execution of the receiving operation, i.e. removal of the matching message, call, reply or exception from the port queue, maybe an assignment of the received information to a variable and the execution of the statement block following the receiving operation.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria of the trigger operation are not
requirements.canonical: In a receiving-branch with a `trigger` operation, the top message of the port queue IS removed also if the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria are not.
requirements.original: In the case of the trigger operation the top message of the queue is also removed if the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria is not.

requirements.subject: ent:trigger-operation
requirements.condition: the Boolean guard is fulfilled but the matching criteria of the trigger operation are not
requirements.canonical: If the Boolean guard of a `trigger` branch is fulfilled but its matching criteria are not, the statement block of that alternative IS NOT executed.
requirements.original: In this case the statement block of the given alternative is not executed.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a snapshot IS described as a series of indivisible actions of a test component.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The TTCN-3 semantics describe the evaluation of a snapshot as a series of indivisible actions of a test component.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 semantics DO NOT assume that the evaluation of a snapshot has no duration.
requirements.original: The semantics do not assume that the evaluation of a snapshot has no duration.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: Events occurring during the evaluation of a snapshot (component stops, timer timeouts, new messages, calls, replies or exceptions entering port queues) DO NOT change the actual snapshot and ARE NOT considered for its evaluation.
requirements.original: During the evaluation of a snapshot, test components may stop, timers may timeout and new messages, calls, replies or exceptions may enter the port queues of the component However, these events do not change the actual snapshot and thus, are not considered for the snapshot evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-branch
requirements.canonical: Due to dynamic test configurations, a receiving-branch CAN refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Due to the possibility of defining dynamic test configurations, a receiving branch may refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port belongs to the receiving component, and matching IS related to the top elements in the port queues.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, ports belong to the receiving component and matching is related to the top elements in the port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A dynamically unmapped or disconnected port contributes to a snapshot in the same manner as a mapped or connected port.
requirements.original: Dynamically unmapped and disconnected ports contribute to a snapshot in the same manner as mapped and connected ports.

requirements.subject: ent:receiving-operation
requirements.canonical: The execution of receiving operations MAY empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.
requirements.original: This means, the execution of receiving operations may empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: no alternative can be selected and executed
requirements.canonical: If none of the alternative branches in an `alt` statement and none of the top alternatives in the invoked altsteps and active defaults can be selected and executed, the `alt` statement SHALL be executed again, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the evaluation of the alternative branches is repeated with the new snapshot.
requirements.original: If none of the alternative branches in the alt statement and top alternatives in the invoked altsteps and active defaults can be selected and executed, the alt statement shall be executed again, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the evaluation of the alternative branches is repeated with the new snapshot.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: The repeated evaluation of an `alt` statement SHALL continue until an alternative branch is selected and executed, the test case is stopped by another component or by the test system, or a dynamic error occurs.
requirements.original: This repetitive procedure shall continue until either an alternative branch is selected and executed, or the test case is stopped by another component or by the test system (e.g. because the MTC is stopped) or with a dynamic error.

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.condition: a test component is completely blocked
requirements.canonical: If a test component is completely blocked, the test case SHALL stop and indicate a dynamic error.
requirements.original: The test case shall stop and indicate a dynamic error if a test component is completely blocked.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component IS completely blocked when none of the alternatives can be chosen, no relevant test component is running, no relevant timer is running and all relevant ports contain at least one message, call, reply or exception that does not match.
requirements.original: This means none of the alternatives can be chosen, no relevant test component is running, no relevant timer is running and all relevant ports contain at least one message, call, reply or exception that do not match.

readings: A test component IS completely blocked when no alternative can be chosen and no test component, timer or port referenced in the alternatives of the alt statement (including invoked altsteps and active defaults) could change the situation.
A test component IS completely blocked when no alternative can be chosen and no test component or timer of the whole test configuration that is relevant to any future event is running.
ambiguity.issue: The term "relevant" for components, timers and ports is not defined; the first reading (relevant = referenced in the alternatives being evaluated) is chosen as most likely.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: The repetitive procedure of taking a complete snapshot and re-evaluating all alternatives IS only a conceptual means for describing the semantics of the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: The repetitive procedure of taking a complete snapshot and re-evaluate all alternatives is only a conceptual means for describing the semantics of the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: The concrete algorithm that implements the `alt` statement semantics IS outside the scope of the TTCN-3 core language standard.
requirements.original: The concrete algorithm that implements this semantics is outside the scope of the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: An alternative MAY be enabled or disabled by a Boolean expression placed between the "[" and "]" brackets of the alternative.
requirements.original: If necessary, it is possible to enable/disable an alternative by means of a Boolean expression placed between the ("[…]") brackets of the alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: Any branch in an `alt` statement MAY be defined as an else-branch by including the `else` keyword between the opening and closing brackets at the beginning of the alternative.
requirements.original: Any branch in an alt statement can be defined as an else branch by including the else keyword between the opening and closing brackets at the beginning of the alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: no textually preceding alternative has proceeded
requirements.canonical: The statement block of an else-branch IS always executed if no other alternative textually preceding the else-branch has proceeded.
requirements.original: The statement block of the else branch is always executed if no other alternative textually preceding the else branch has proceeded.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the @nodefault modifier is not present
requirements.canonical: Unless the `@nodefault` modifier is present, the default mechanism IS always invoked at the end of all alternatives of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: It should be noted that the default mechanism (see clause 20.5) is always invoked at the end of all alternatives unless the @nodefault modifier is present.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: an else-branch is defined
requirements.canonical: If an else-branch is defined in an `alt` statement, the default mechanism IS NOT called, i.e. active defaults are never entered.
requirements.original: If an else branch is defined, the default mechanism will never be called, i.e. active defaults will never be entered.

readings: If an else-branch is defined in an alt statement, the default mechanism IS NOT called for that alt statement at all.
If an else-branch is reached in an alt statement, the default mechanism IS NOT called; alternatives preceding the else-branch still have priority.
ambiguity.issue: Since the else-branch is always taken when reached, both readings give the same observable effect; the first, literal reading is chosen. It is unclear whether an else-branch inside an invoked altstep also suppresses the defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY contain an else-branch.
requirements.original: NOTE 4: It is also possible to use else in altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.canonical: An else-branch MAY contain a `repeat` statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 5: It is allowed to use a repeat statement within an else branch.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement or an altstep MAY define more than one else-branch.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: It is allowed to define more than one else branch in an alt statement or in an altstep, however always only the first else branch is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:else-branch
requirements.condition: more than one else-branch is defined
requirements.canonical: If an `alt` statement or altstep contains more than one else-branch, only the first else-branch IS ever executed.
requirements.original: NOTE 6: It is allowed to define more than one else branch in an alt statement or in an altstep, however always only the first else branch is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: The re-evaluation of an `alt` statement CAN be specified by a `repeat` statement.
requirements.original: The re-evaluation of an alt statement can be specified by using a repeat statement (see clause 20.3).

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be invoked as an alternative in an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the invocation of altsteps as alternatives in alt statements (see clause 16.2.1).

requirements.subject: ent:statement-block
requirements.condition: an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative and one of its alternatives is selected
requirements.canonical: When an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative, the optional statement block following the altstep call SHALL also be executed.
requirements.original: When an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative, the optional statement block following the altstep call shall also be executed.

readings: When an alternative of an explicitly invoked altstep is selected and executed, the optional statement block following the altstep call SHALL also be executed.
Whenever an altstep is explicitly invoked as an alternative, the optional statement block following the altstep call SHALL be executed, regardless of whether an altstep alternative was selected.
ambiguity.issue: The sentence omits the condition stated in 20.2-s024; the first reading (consistent with 20.2-s024) is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the `alt` statement when a branch of the `alt` statement or of an invoked default is selected and completely executed.
requirements.original: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the alt statement when one of the branches of the alt or invoked defaults is selected and completely executed, or a branch of an altstep used in an altsteps-branch is selected and the branch and the optional statement block following the invoked altstep are completely executed.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.canonical: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the `alt` statement when a branch of an altstep used in an altstep-branch is selected and both that branch and the optional statement block following the invoked altstep are completely executed.
requirements.original: Behaviour execution continues with the statement following the alt statement when one of the branches of the alt or invoked defaults is selected and completely executed, or a branch of an altstep used in an altsteps-branch is selected and the branch and the optional statement block following the invoked altstep are completely executed.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: a break statement is reached in the selected branch
requirements.canonical: Execution continues with the statement following the `alt` statement if a `break` statement is reached in the statement block of the selected branch of the `alt` statement, of an altstep used in an altstep-branch, or of an altstep invoked as default.
requirements.original: Execution also continues with the statement following the alt statement if a break statement is reached in the statement block of the selected branch of an alt statement, of an altstep used in an altstep-branch, or of an `altstep` invoked as default.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement MAY be left by a `goto` statement in the selected branch of the `alt` statement, and execution continues with the statement following the label the `goto` points to.
requirements.original: The alt statement can also be left by using a goto statement in the selected branch of the alt (i.e. no branches of altsteps and defaults can be considered in this case), and execution continues with the statement following the label, `goto` is pointing to.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement CANNOT be used to leave an `alt` statement from a branch of an altstep or default.
requirements.original: The alt statement can also be left by using a goto statement in the selected branch of the alt (i.e. no branches of altsteps and defaults can be considered in this case), and execution continues with the statement following the label, `goto` is pointing to.

readings: A `goto` statement in a branch of an altstep or default SHALL NOT be used to leave the alt statement.
When an alt statement is left with `goto`, no altstep or default branches are evaluated (they are bypassed) since the goto is in a branch of the alt itself.
ambiguity.issue: The parenthesis "(i.e. no branches of altsteps and defaults can be considered in this case)" can be read as a restriction or as a consequence; the restriction reading is chosen, consistent with goto restrictions in 19.6.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The open and close square brackets "[" "]" SHALL be present at the start of each alternative of an `alt` statement, even if they are empty.
requirements.original: a) The open and close square brackets ("[…]") shall be present at the start of each alternative, even if they are empty.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The mandatory square brackets at the start of each alternative ARE necessary to syntactically distinguish one alternative from another and aid readability.
requirements.original: This not only aids readability but also is necessary to syntactically distinguish one alternative from another.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of a Boolean expression guarding an alternative SHALL NOT have side effects.
requirements.original: b) The evaluation of a Boolean expression guarding an alternative shall not have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:boolean-guard
requirements.canonical: A Boolean guard expression SHALL obey the same restrictions as the initialization of local definitions within altsteps and the restrictions on the contents of functions called from special places.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component, the same restrictions as the restrictions for the initialization of local definitions within altsteps (clause 16.1.5) and the restrictions imposed on the contents of functions called from special places (clause 16.1.4) shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-branch
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of the event of an alt branch SHALL NOT have side effects.
requirements.original: c) The evaluation of the event of an alt branch shall not have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: An expression occurring in the matching part of an alternative SHALL obey the restrictions on the contents of functions called from special places.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects that cause an inconsistency between the actual snapshot and the state of the component or introduce indeterminism in the evaluation of the following alt branches or the re-evaluation of the same alt branch, the restrictions imposed on the contents of functions called from special places (clause 16.1.4) shall apply to expressions occurring in the matching part of an alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep-branch
requirements.condition: none of the alternatives in the altstep is chosen
requirements.canonical: If none of the alternatives of an altstep invoked from an alt branch is chosen, the evaluation of that altstep SHALL NOT have side effects.
requirements.original: d) The evaluation of an altstep invoked from an alt branch, if none of the alternatives in the altstep is chosen, shall not have side effects.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: An actual parameter of an altstep invoked from an alt branch SHALL obey the restrictions on the contents of functions called from special places.
requirements.original: To avoid side effects the restrictions imposed on the contents of functions called from special places (clause 16.1.4) shall apply to the actual parameters of the invoked altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.condition: the alt statement is used inside control behaviour
requirements.canonical: An `alt` statement used inside control behaviour SHALL only contain timeout statements as alternatives.
requirements.original: f) An alt statement used inside control behaviour shall only contain timeout statements.

readings: An alt statement in control behaviour SHALL have only timeout-branches (and possibly else-branches).
An alt statement in control behaviour SHALL have only timeout-branches; else-branches and altstep-branches are also forbidden.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether else-branches (and altstep-branches whose altsteps only contain timeouts) are permitted; the first reading is chosen. "timeout statements" refers to timeout operations.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement IS used for a re-evaluation of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The repeat statement is used for a re-evaluation of an alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement has the syntax `repeat`.
requirements.original: repeat

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.condition: used in a statement block of an alt alternative
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement in the statement block of an alternative of an `alt` statement causes the re-evaluation of the `alt` statement, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the alternatives are evaluated in the order of their specification.
requirements.original: The repeat statement, when used in the statement block of alternatives of alt statements, causes the re-evaluation of the alt statement, i.e. a new snapshot is taken and the alternatives of the alt statement are evaluated in the order of their specification.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.condition: used in the response and exception handling part of a blocking call
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement in a statement block of the response and exception handling part of a blocking procedure call causes the re-evaluation of the response and exception handling part of the call.
requirements.original: When used in statement blocks of the response and exception handling parts of blocking procedure calls, the repeat statement causes the re-evaluation of the response and exception handling part of the call (see clause 22.3.1).

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.condition: used in a top alternative of an altstep
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement in a top alternative of an altstep definition causes a new snapshot and the re-evaluation of the `alt` statement from which the altstep has been called.
requirements.original: If a repeat statement is used in a top alternative in an altstep definition, it causes a new snapshot and the re-evaluation of the alt statement from which the altstep has been called.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep containing a `repeat` statement MAY be called either implicitly by the default mechanism or explicitly in an `alt` statement, with the same re-evaluation effect.
requirements.original: The call of the altstep may either be done implicitly by the default mechanism (see clause 20.5.1) or explicitly in the alt statement (see clause 20.2).

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: A `repeat` statement SHALL only be used within `alt` statements, `call` statements or altsteps.
requirements.original: a) The repeat statement shall only be used within alt statements, call statements or altsteps.

improper_terms.proper: response and exception handling part of a blocking call operation

ambiguity.issue: "call statements" is not a defined term; 20.3-s004 restricts the use to the response and exception handling part of blocking procedure calls.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The `interleave` statement specifies the interleaved occurrence and handling of the receiving events `done`, `killed`, `timeout`, `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` and `check`.
requirements.original: The `interleave` statement allows to specify the interleaved occurrence and handling of receiving events including `done`, `killed`, `timeout`, `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch` and `check`.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The `interleave` statement has the syntax `interleave [@nodefault] { { [] (TimeoutStatement | ReceiveStatement | TriggerStatement | GetCallStatement | CatchStatement | CheckStatement | GetReplyStatement | DoneStatement | KilledStatement) StatementBlock } }`.
requirements.original:
interleave [ @nodefault ] "{" 
     { "[]" ( TimeoutStatement |
          ReceiveStatement |
          TriggerStatement |
          GetCallStatement |
          CatchStatement |
          CheckStatement |
          GetReplyStatement |
          DoneStatement |
          KilledStatement ) StatementBlock
     } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: Each branch of an `interleave` statement SHALL start with a reception statement (`timeout`, `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `catch`, `check`, `getreply`, `done` or `killed`) followed by a statement block.
requirements.original:
interleave [ @nodefault ] "{" 
     { "[]" ( TimeoutStatement |
          ReceiveStatement |
          TriggerStatement |
          GetCallStatement |
          CatchStatement |
          CheckStatement |
          GetReplyStatement |
          DoneStatement |
          KilledStatement ) StatementBlock
     } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: Interleaved behaviour CAN always be replaced by an equivalent set of nested `alt` statements.
requirements.original: Interleaved behaviour can always be replaced by an equivalent set of nested alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: a reception statement in an interleave statement is executed
requirements.canonical: Whenever a reception statement within an `interleave` statement is executed, the following non-reception statements ARE executed subsequently until the next reception statement is reached, a `break` statement is reached, or the interleaved sequence ends.
requirements.original: a) Whenever a reception statement is executed, the following non-reception statements are subsequently executed until the next reception statement is reached, a break statement is reached, or the interleaved sequence ends.

requirements.subject: ent:reception-statement
requirements.canonical: A reception statement IS a TTCN-3 statement that may occur in sets of alternatives, i.e. `receive`, `check`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`, `done`, `killed` and `timeout`.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Reception statements are TTCN-3 statements which may occur in sets of alternatives, i.e. `receive`, `check`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `getreply`, `catch`, `done`, `killed` and `timeout`.

requirements.subject: ent:non-reception-statement
requirements.canonical: A non-reception statement IS any other non-control-transfer statement that can be used within the `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: Non-reception statements denote all other non-control-transfer statements which can be used within the `interleave` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: none of the alternatives of the interleave statement can be executed
requirements.canonical: If none of the alternatives of the `interleave` statement can be executed, the default mechanism IS invoked.
requirements.original: b) If none of the alternatives of the `interleave` statement can be executed, the default mechanism will be invoked.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the default mechanism is invoked from an interleave statement
requirements.canonical: When the default mechanism is invoked from an `interleave` statement, the actual snapshot IS used to evaluate the altsteps that have been activated as defaults before entering the `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: This means, according to the semantics of the default mechanism, the actual snapshot will be used to evaluate those altsteps that have been activated before entering the `interleave` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.condition: the interleave statement contains the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: If an `interleave` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, all active default alternatives ARE ignored for the execution of that `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: If the `interleave` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, all active default alternatives are ignored for the execution of this `interleave` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The complete semantics of the default mechanism within an `interleave` statement IS given by replacing the `interleave` statement by an equivalent set of nested `alt` statements.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The complete semantics of the default mechanism within an `interleave` statement is given by replacing the `interleave` statement by an equivalent set of nested alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: the interleave statement contains the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement with the `@nodefault` modifier IS equivalent to a set of replacement `alt` statements that all have the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.original: If the `interleave` statement contains the `@nodefault` modifier, it is equivalent with all replacement `alt` statement having the `@nodefault` modifier.

ambiguity.issue: 'all replacement alt statement having' mixes singular/plural; meaning is that every replacement alt statement carries @nodefault.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism applies to each of the replacement `alt` statements of an `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: The default mechanism applies for each of these alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: no break statement was encountered
requirements.canonical: If no `break` statement was encountered, the evaluation of the `interleave` statement continues by taking the next snapshot.
requirements.original: c) The evaluation then continues by taking the next snapshot if no break statement was encountered.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: a break statement is executed
requirements.canonical: The evaluation of an `interleave` statement IS terminated if a `break` statement is executed.
requirements.original: d) The evaluation of the interleave statement is terminated if a break statement is executed.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain the control transfer statements `activate`, `deactivate`, `repeat`, any call of an altstep, or any direct or indirect call of a user-defined function that includes reception statements.
requirements.original: a) Control transfer statements activate, deactivate, repeat, all calls of altsteps and (direct and indirect) calls of user-defined functions, which include reception statements, shall not be present in interleave statements.

readings: An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain `activate`, `deactivate`, `repeat`, any altstep call, or any (direct or indirect) call of a user-defined function that includes reception statements.
An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain `activate`, `deactivate`, `repeat`, or calls of altsteps or user-defined functions where any of these include reception statements.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of the relative clause 'which include reception statements' is unclear (only functions, or also altsteps / all listed items); first reading chosen because altsteps always contain reception statements. Also 'activate' and 'deactivate' are operations, not control transfer statements.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: A branch of an `interleave` statement SHALL NOT be guarded by a Boolean expression, i.e. the `[ ]` SHALL always be empty.
requirements.original: b) In addition, it is not allowed to guard branches of an interleave statement with Boolean expressions (i.e. the '[ ]' shall always be empty).

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement SHALL NOT contain an `else` branch.
requirements.original: It is also not allowed to specify else branches in interleaved behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.condition: the interleave statement is used inside control behaviour
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement used inside control behaviour SHALL only contain `timeout` statements in the event parts of its alternatives.
requirements.original: c) An interleave used inside control behaviour shall only contain timeout statements in the event parts of the alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The control transfer statements `for`, `while`, `do-while` and `goto` MAY be used within `interleave` statements under the conditions stated in 20.4 restriction d).
requirements.original: d) The restricted use of the control transfer statements for, while, do-while, and goto within interleave statements is allowed under the following conditions:

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.condition: the statement block does not contain reception statements
requirements.canonical: The loop statements `for`, `while` and `do-while` MAY be used within an `interleave` statement only in statement blocks that do not contain reception statements.
requirements.original: The loop statements for, while, and do-while can be used within statements blocks that do not contain reception statements.

requirements.subject: ent:for-statement
requirements.canonical: A `for`, `while` or `do-while` statement SHALL NOT be used within an `interleave` statement in a statement block that contains reception statements.
requirements.original: The loop statements for, while, and do-while can be used within statements blocks that do not contain reception statements.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.condition: the statement blocks do not contain reception statements
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement MAY be used within an `interleave` statement for jumps within statement blocks that do not contain reception statements.
requirements.original: The goto statement can be used for defining jumps with statements blocks that do not contain reception statements and for specifying jumps out of interleave statements.

readings: A `goto` statement MAY jump only between positions inside statement blocks that contain no reception statements.
A `goto` statement MAY be placed in a statement block without reception statements and jump to any label of the interleave statement.
ambiguity.issue: 'jumps with statements blocks' is garbled ('within'?); it is unclear whether the jump target must also lie in a block without reception statements. First reading chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A `goto` statement MAY be used to jump out of an `interleave` statement.
requirements.original: The goto statement can be used for defining jumps with statements blocks that do not contain reception statements and for specifying jumps out of interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be activated as a default.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the activation of altsteps (see clause 16.2.1) as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: Each test component stores its defaults, i.e. its activated altsteps, as an ordered list.
requirements.original: For each test component the defaults, i.e. activated altsteps, are stored as an ordered list.

requirements.subject: ent:list-of-defaults
requirements.canonical: The list of defaults IS ordered in reverse order of activation, i.e. the last activated default is the first element in the list.
requirements.original: The defaults are listed in the reversed order of their activation i.e. the last activated default is the first element in the list of active defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `activate` and `deactivate` operations operate on the list of defaults.
requirements.original: The TTCN-3 operations activate (see clause 20.5.2) and deactivate (see clause 20.5.3) operate on the list of defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation creates a new default
requirements.canonical: If an `activate` operation creates a new default, the new default IS inserted as the first element into the list of defaults.
requirements.original: If an activate operation creates a new default, it is inserted as the first element into the list.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the default was previously suspended and is re-activated
requirements.canonical: A re-activated default that was previously suspended retains its position in the list of defaults.
requirements.original: Re-activated defaults that were previously suspended retain their position in the list.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `deactivate` operation either removes a default from the list of defaults or suspends it, in which case the default remains in the list but is temporarily inactive.
requirements.original: The deactivate operation either removes a default from the list or suspends it in which case the default remains in the list, but is temporarily inactive.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default in the list of defaults IS identified by a default reference generated as the result of the corresponding `activate` operation.
requirements.original: A default in the default list can be identified by means of default reference that is generated as a result of the corresponding activate operation.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: no alternative of the alt statement could be executed in the actual snapshot
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism IS evoked at the end of each `alt` statement not annotated with the `@nodefault` modifier, if due to the actual snapshot none of the specified alternatives could be executed.
requirements.original: The default mechanism is evoked at the end of each alt statement not annotated with the @nodefault modifier, if due to the actual snapshot none of the specified alternatives could be executed.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the alt statement has the @nodefault modifier
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism IS NOT evoked at the end of an `alt` statement annotated with the `@nodefault` modifier.
requirements.original: The default mechanism is evoked at the end of each alt statement not annotated with the @nodefault modifier, if due to the actual snapshot none of the specified alternatives could be executed.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: An evoked default mechanism invokes the first altstep in the list of defaults, i.e. the last activated default, and waits for the result of its termination.
requirements.original: An evoked default mechanism invokes the first altstep in the list of defaults, i.e. the last activated default, and waits for the result of its termination.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: The termination of a default invoked by the default mechanism IS either successful or unsuccessful.
requirements.original: The termination can be successful or unsuccessful.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: The termination of a default IS unsuccessful if none of the top alternatives of the altstep defining the default behaviour could be selected.
requirements.original: Unsuccessful means that none of the top alternatives of the altstep (see clause 16.2.1) defining the default behaviour could be selected, successful means that one of the top alternatives of the default has been selected and executed.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: The termination of a default IS successful if one of the top alternatives of the default has been selected and executed.
requirements.original: Unsuccessful means that none of the top alternatives of the altstep (see clause 16.2.1) defining the default behaviour could be selected, successful means that one of the top alternatives of the default has been selected and executed.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: An `interleave` statement IS semantically equivalent to a nested set of `alt` statements, and the default mechanism applies to each of these `alt` statements.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: An interleave statement is semantically equivalent to a nested set of alt statements and the default mechanism also applies to each of these alt statements.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism applies to `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: This means, the default mechanism also applies to interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: The restrictions imposed on `interleave` statements in clause 20.4 do not apply to altsteps activated as default behaviour for `interleave` statements.
requirements.original: Furthermore, the restrictions imposed on interleave statements in clause 20.4 do not apply to altsteps that are activated as default behaviour for interleave statements.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An alternative in an altstep activated as a default CAN refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Due to the possibility of defining dynamic test configurations, an alternative in an altstep activated as default may refer to a disconnected or unmapped port at the time of its evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port belongs to the receiving component, and matching relates to the top elements of the port queues.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, ports belong to the receiving component and matching is related to the top elements in the port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A dynamically unmapped or disconnected port contributes to a snapshot in the same manner as a mapped or connected port.
requirements.original: Dynamically unmapped and disconnected ports contribute to a snapshot in the same manner as mapped and connected ports.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep invoked as a default CAN execute receiving operations that empty the queues of unmapped or disconnected ports without causing a test case error.
requirements.original: This means, an altstep invoked as default may execute receiving operations that empty the queues of unmapped and disconnected ports without causing a test case error.

ambiguity.issue: 'test case error' is a glossary term; the text uses it correctly but the receiving operations are elsewhere called 'reception statements'.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the invoked default terminated unsuccessfully
requirements.canonical: In the case of an unsuccessful termination of a default, the default mechanism invokes the next default in the list of defaults that is not in the suspended state.
requirements.original: In the case of an unsuccessful termination, the default mechanism invokes the next default in the list that is not in the suspended state.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the last default in the list terminated unsuccessfully
requirements.canonical: If the last default in the list of defaults has terminated unsuccessfully, the default mechanism returns to the end of the `alt` statement in which it was invoked and indicates an unsuccessful default execution.
requirements.original: If the last default in the list has terminated unsuccessfully, the default mechanism will return to the place in the alt statement in which it has been invoked, i.e. at the end of the alt statement, and indicate an unsuccessful default execution.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the list of defaults is empty or contains only suspended defaults
requirements.canonical: The default mechanism indicates an unsuccessful default execution if the list of defaults is empty or contains only suspended defaults.
requirements.original: An unsuccessful default execution will also be indicated if the list of defaults is empty or if it contains only suspended defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the default execution was unsuccessful
requirements.canonical: An unsuccessful default execution causes a new snapshot to be taken, or a dynamic error if the test component is blocked.
requirements.original: An unsuccessful default execution may cause a new snapshot or a dynamic error if the test component is blocked (see clause 20.1).

readings: After an unsuccessful default execution a new snapshot IS taken, unless the test component is blocked, in which case a dynamic error occurs.
After an unsuccessful default execution a new snapshot or a dynamic error MAY occur, at the discretion of the implementation.
ambiguity.issue: 'may cause' could be read as implementation freedom; clause 20.1 indicates the first reading (error only when blocked), which is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the default terminated successfully
requirements.canonical: After a successful termination, a default CAN stop the test component by means of a `stop` statement.
requirements.original: In the case of a successful termination, the default may either stop the test component by means of a stop statement, or the main control flow of the test component will continue immediately after the alt statement from which the default mechanism was called or the test component will take new snapshot and re-evaluate the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the default terminated successfully
requirements.canonical: After a successful termination of a default that does not stop the test component, the main control flow of the test component either continues immediately after the `alt` statement from which the default mechanism was called, or the test component takes a new snapshot and re-evaluates the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: In the case of a successful termination, the default may either stop the test component by means of a stop statement, or the main control flow of the test component will continue immediately after the alt statement from which the default mechanism was called or the test component will take new snapshot and re-evaluate the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: Re-evaluation of the `alt` statement after a successful default termination SHALL be specified by means of a `repeat` statement in the default.
requirements.original: The latter has to be specified by means of a repeat statement (see clause 20.3).

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the selected top alternative ends with break or without repeat
requirements.canonical: If the execution of the selected top alternative of a default ends with a `break` statement or without a `repeat` statement, the control flow of the test component continues immediately after the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: If the execution of the selected top alternative of the default ends with a break statement or without a repeat statement the control flow of the test component will continue immediately after the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language does not restrict the implementation of the default mechanism.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: TTCN-3 does not restrict the implementation of the default mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool MAY implement the default mechanism as a process implicitly called at the end of each `alt` statement or as a separate thread responsible for default handling.
requirements.original: It may for example be implemented in form of a process that is implicitly called at the end of each alt statement or in form of a separate thread that is only responsible for the default handling.

requirements.subject: ent:default-mechanism
requirements.condition: the default mechanism has been invoked
requirements.canonical: When the default mechanism has been invoked, the defaults SHALL be called in the reverse order of their activation.
requirements.original: The only requirement is that defaults are called in the reverse order of their activation when the default mechanism has been invoked.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `activate` operation IS used to activate altsteps as defaults.
requirements.original: The activate operation is used to activate altsteps as defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `activate` operation has the syntax `activate ( AltstepRef ( [ActualPar {, ActualPar}] ) | ObjectReference )`.
requirements.original: activate "(" AltstepRef "(" [ { ActualPar [","] } ] ")" | ObjectReference ")"

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an AltstepRef
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an AltstepRef puts the referenced altstep as the first element into the list of defaults.
requirements.original: An activate operation if it is called with an AltstepRef will put the referenced altstep as the first element into the list of defaults and return a default reference.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an AltstepRef
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an AltstepRef returns a default reference.
requirements.original: An activate operation if it is called with an AltstepRef will put the referenced altstep as the first element into the list of defaults and return a default reference.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS a unique identifier for the default.
requirements.original: The default reference is a unique identifier for the default and may be used in a deactivate operation for the deactivation of the default.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference MAY be used in a `deactivate` operation to deactivate the default.
requirements.original: The default reference is a unique identifier for the default and may be used in a deactivate operation for the deactivation of the default.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the altstep is parameterized
requirements.canonical: The actual parameters of a parameterized altstep that is activated as a default SHALL be provided in the corresponding `activate` operation.
requirements.original: The actual parameters of a parameterized altstep (see clause 16.2.1) that should be activated as a default, shall be provided in the corresponding activate statement.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'activate statement' although activate is an operation.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameters of an altstep activated as a default ARE bound to the default at the time of its activation, not at the time of its invocation by the default mechanism.
requirements.original: This means, the actual parameters are bound to the default at the time of its activation (and not e.g. at the time of its invocation by the default mechanism).

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an ObjectReference re-activates the referenced default that was previously suspended by a `deactivate` operation.
requirements.original: If the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference, it will re-activate the referenced default which was previously suspended by a deactivate operation.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference
requirements.canonical: A default re-activated by an `activate` operation with an ObjectReference SHALL remain in the same place in the list of defaults as before the `activate` operation.
requirements.original: In this case the referenced default shall remain in the same place in the list of defaults as it was before the activate operation, and the activate operation shall return with the same _ObjectReference as it received at calling._

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.condition: the activate operation is called with an ObjectReference
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation called with an ObjectReference SHALL return the same ObjectReference as it received at calling.
requirements.original: In this case the referenced default shall remain in the same place in the list of defaults as it was before the activate operation, and the activate operation shall return with the same _ObjectReference as it received at calling._

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: The effect of an `activate` operation IS local to the test component in which it is called.
requirements.original: The effect of an activate operation is local to the test component in which it is called.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component CANNOT activate a default in another test component.
requirements.original: This means, a test component cannot activate a default in another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: An `activate` operation MAY be called without saving the returned default reference.
requirements.original: The activate operation can be called without saving the returned default reference.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: A default that is not explicitly deactivated IS deactivated implicitly at MTC termination.
requirements.original: This form is useful in test cases which do not require explicit deactivation of the activated default, i.e. deactivation of a default is done implicitly at MTC termination.

readings: Defaults not explicitly deactivated are deactivated implicitly when the MTC (and thus the test case) terminates.
Defaults not explicitly deactivated are deactivated implicitly when the test component owning them terminates.
ambiguity.issue: Defaults are local to each test component, so for a PTC the deactivation at 'MTC termination' is unclear; first reading kept as literal text. Also 'test cases' vs glossary 'test case'.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.condition: the altstep is activated as a default
requirements.canonical: An altstep that is activated as a default SHALL only have `in` formal parameters.
requirements.original: c) An altstep that is activated as a default shall only have in parameters.

readings: An altstep activated as a default SHALL only have `in` value or template parameters, apart from port and timer parameters, which are always passed by reference.
An altstep activated as a default SHALL NOT have any port, timer, `out` or `inout` parameters.
ambiguity.issue: EXAMPLE 3 (20.5.2-s024) activates an altstep with port and timer parameters, which are not `in` parameters; first reading chosen to stay consistent with the example.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `activate` operation SHALL be of `default` type.
requirements.original: d) The ObjectReference shall be of default type.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of an `activate` operation SHALL refer to a default that is marked as suspended in the list of defaults.
requirements.original: e) The ObjectReference shall refer to a default that is marked as suspended in the list of defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `deactivate` operation IS used to deactivate or suspend defaults, i.e. previously activated altsteps.
requirements.original: The deactivate operation is used to deactivate or suspend defaults, i.e. previously activated altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.canonical: The `deactivate` operation has the syntax `deactivate [ ( ObjectReference [, Expression] ) ]`.
requirements.original: deactivate [ "(" ObjectReference [ "," Expression ] ")" ]

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.condition: the optional Expression evaluates to false
requirements.canonical: If the optional Expression evaluates to `false`, a `deactivate` operation removes the referenced default from the list of defaults.
requirements.original: A deactivate operation will remove the referenced default from the list of defaults if the optional Expression evaluates to false, otherwise it marks the referenced default in the list of defaults as suspended.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.condition: the optional Expression evaluates to true
requirements.canonical: If the optional Expression evaluates to `true`, a `deactivate` operation marks the referenced default in the list of defaults as suspended.
requirements.original: A deactivate operation will remove the referenced default from the list of defaults if the optional Expression evaluates to false, otherwise it marks the referenced default in the list of defaults as suspended.

requirements.subject: ent:default
requirements.canonical: A suspended default CAN be re-activated by an `activate` operation.
requirements.original: NOTE: A suspended default can be re-activated by an activate operation.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.canonical: The effect of a `deactivate` operation IS local to the test component in which it is called.
requirements.original: The effect of a deactivate operation is local to the test component in which it is called.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component CANNOT deactivate or suspend a default in another test component.
requirements.original: This means, a test component cannot deactivate or suspend a default in another test component.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.condition: the deactivate operation has no parameter
requirements.canonical: A `deactivate` operation without parameters deactivates all defaults of the test component.
requirements.original: A deactivate operation without parameter deactivates all defaults of a test component.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.condition: the ObjectReference is null
requirements.canonical: A `deactivate` operation called with the special value `null` as its ObjectReference has no effect.
requirements.original: Calling a deactivate operation with the special value null as its ObjectReference has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.condition: the default reference is undefined
requirements.canonical: A `deactivate` operation called with an undefined default reference, e.g. a reference to an already deactivated default or an uninitialized default reference variable, SHALL cause a runtime error.
requirements.original: Calling a deactivate operation with an undefined default reference, e.g. an old reference to a default that has already been deactivated or an uninitialized default reference variable, shall cause a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `deactivate` operation SHALL be of `default` type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of default type.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The optional Expression of a `deactivate` operation SHALL be of `boolean` type.
requirements.original: b) The optional Expression shall be of boolean type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The optional Expression of a `deactivate` operation SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: b) The optional Expression shall be of boolean type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:expression
requirements.canonical: The default value of the optional Expression of a `deactivate` operation IS `false`.
